tagline: Live translated subtitles for anything you watch.

@tagline.description: Under the app's name, where it introduces itself.

mygo.appDescription: Live translated subtitles for anything you watch

@statusPreparing.description: Where the subtitles show, while recognition starts.

statusDownloading: Downloading speech recognition for this language…

@statusDownloading.description: Where the subtitles show, while the system downloads recognition for the spoken language (about 20 s).

statusNoPermission: Tomoru can't hear your Mac. Allow it in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Screen & System Audio Recording.

@statusNoPermission.description: Where the subtitles show, when the System Audio Recording permission is off. Name the settings as System Settings does in the language.

@statusStopped.description: Where the subtitles show, when translating stopped on an error.

@translationFailed.description: Under a subtitle line whose translation failed.

translationFailedCloud: Index-Translate's cloud isn't answering. Try again later, or choose a local model or your own API in Settings › Speech & translation.

@translationFailedCloud.description: In the first-run guide, under the translation check, when lines failed to translate with Index-Translate's cloud: it may be down.

@translationSkipped.description: Under a subtitle line, and in the history, when its translation was skipped because translating fell behind.

translationKeyRefused: The translation API refused the key. Check it in Settings › Speech & translation.

@translationKeyRefused.description: Under a subtitle line whose translation failed because the translation API refused the API key (HTTP 401 or 403).

translationLimited: The translation API is limiting requests, or the quota is used up.

@translationLimited.description: Under a subtitle line whose translation failed because the translation API is rate limiting, or the account's quota or balance ran out (HTTP 429 or 402).

@translationNotAnswering.description: Under a subtitle line whose translation failed because the translation service could not be reached or did not answer in time.

@spokenLanguage.description: Label of the menu of the language spoken in the video.

@translateInto.description: Label of the menu of the language to translate into.

@swapLanguages.description: Button that swaps the spoken language and the one to translate into.

@source.description: Label of the menu of what to hear: all the system's sound, or one app's.

@sourceAll.description: In the menu of what to hear: everything the computer plays.

@sourcePlaying.description: Heading in the menu of what to hear, over the apps playing sound now.

@sourceOtherApps.description: Heading in the menu of what to hear, over the other running apps.

@sourceNotRunning.description: In the menu of what to hear: the app chosen, which is not running now.

@shortcut.description: Label of the global shortcut that starts and stops translating.

@shortcutRecording.description: In the shortcut field while it records a new global shortcut, before any key is pressed.

@shortcutChange.description: Tooltip of the shortcut field, whose keycaps a click records anew.

@shortcutNeedsModifier.description: Under the shortcut field, when the keys pressed have no Control, Option or Command.

shortcutTaken: {keys} can't be used; another app may have it

@shortcutTaken.description: Under the shortcut field, when the system refused the shortcut pressed.

@uiLanguage.description: Label of the menu of the language the app's own words are in.

@uiLanguageSystem.description: In the menu of the app's language: follow the system's.

@prefsNetwork.description: A card's title in Preferences: how the app reaches the cloud.

@useProxy.description: A switch in Preferences: reach the cloud through a proxy.

useProxyDesc: Cloud recognition and translation, and model downloads, go through it. Models on this computer don't.

@useProxyDesc.description: Under the switch that uses a proxy: what goes through it.

@proxyAddress.description: A field's name in Preferences: the address of the user's proxy.

@proxySystem.description: Under the proxy address: empty, the system's proxy is used, which is this one.

proxySystemNone: Empty for the system's proxy; the system has none set now.

@proxySystemNone.description: Under the proxy address: empty, the system's proxy is used, and the system has none.

proxyInvalid: Not a proxy address, such as 127.0.0.1:7890 or socks5://127.0.0.1:1080: the system's proxy is used.

@proxyInvalid.description: Under the proxy address, when what is typed is no address.

@tabEngines.description: A page of the settings, and a step of the first-run guide: speech recognition and translation.

@styleLabel.description: Label of the subtitles' style: on a box, or text alone.

@styleBox.description: A subtitle style: on a dark box, as closed captions.

@styleImmersive.description: A subtitle style: the text alone, as a film's.

@edgeLabel.description: Label of what goes around the subtitles' letters.

@edgeColor.description: Label of the text edge's color.

@srcSize.description: Label of the size of the original text.

@tgtSize.description: Label of the size of the translation.

@srcColor.description: Label of the color of the original text.

@tgtColor.description: Label of the color of the translation.

@customColor.description: Name of the swatch after the preset colors that opens a color picker, for any color.

@colorScheme.description: Label of the row of color schemes of the subtitles, each setting the colors of the original, the translation and the edge.

@schemeClassic.description: A color scheme: white original, light yellow translation, black edge. The default.

@schemeIce.description: A color scheme: white original, light blue translation, navy edge.

@schemeAmber.description: A color scheme: white original, light orange translation, dark brown edge.

@schemeSakura.description: A color scheme, after cherry blossoms: white original, light pink translation, dark plum edge.

@schemeMint.description: A color scheme: white original, light green translation, black edge.

@schemeFocus.description: A color scheme: gray original and white translation, which stands out. Keep it short: it is the tooltip of a small swatch.

@displayLabel.description: Label of what the subtitles show.

@displayTgt.description: The subtitles show the translation alone.

@displaySrc.description: The subtitles show the original alone, and nothing is translated.

@displaySrcDesc.description: Under what the subtitles show, with the original only.

@shownLabel.description: Label of how many sentences show at once.

@shownFewer.description: Button: show one sentence fewer at once.

@shownMore.description: Button: show one sentence more at once.

@hideAfterLabel.description: A switch: the subtitles go when no new ones come for a few seconds. The app hears the computer's sound, not people, so it names subtitles, not speech.

@hideWait.description: A setting under Hide when nobody speaks: how many seconds the subtitles stay first.

@hideWaitLess.description: Button: hide the subtitles one second sooner.

@hideWaitMore.description: Button: hide the subtitles one second later.

@adjustPosition.description: Button that shows the subtitles' frame to move them.

@resetStyle.description: Button that sets the subtitles' look back to the defaults.

@enginesAsr.description: Heading: the engines that turn speech into text.

@engineApple.description: The name of Apple's speech recognition.

@tagLocal.description: A tag: it runs on this computer.

@tagBuiltIn.description: A tag: it comes with the system.

engineAppleDescription: Fast. Good at Japanese, English, Korean.

@tagCloud.description: A tag: it runs on a server.

@tagRecommended.description: A tag beside the name of the local translation model to pick, Index-Translate 9B. One short word.

engineCloudThanks: Free, thanks to the bilibili team

@engineCloudThanks.description: In the settings, under Index-Translate 35B in the cloud's list: thanks to the team that serves it free. A few words: a Star button is beside it.

cloudSendsText: The cloud service you choose receives the recognized text.

@cloudSendsText.description: Under the cloud's translation services, in the settings and the guide: what leaves the computer. One short line.

@draftLabel.description: A setting's name: translating sentences before they end.

draftDesc: Shows an early draft before a sentence ends

@draftDesc.description: Under Translate ahead, on one line: what it does.

aboutCredits: Translation model Index-Translate (bilibili, Apache-2.0) · UI MyGo · Icons Lucide (ISC)

@aboutCredits.description: In About: the works the app is built on, with their licenses.

@aboutGuide.description: About: the row of the first-run guide, beside the button running it again.

@aboutRerun.description: About: the button running the first-run guide again.

@aboutLogs.description: About: the row of the log files, beside the button showing them in Finder, to attach to a report.

@shortcutHint.description: At the bottom of the menu bar panel.

@aboutTomoru.description: The menu bar icon's menu: opens the About page.

@quitTomoru.description: Menu bar panel, the last icon's tooltip, and the menu bar icon's menu: quits the app.

@settings.description: The settings button on the subtitles' toolbar, as a tooltip.

dragHint: Drag here to place the subtitles

@dragHint.description: On the hovered subtitle area, while it is empty.

adjustHint: The subtitles go here · point here to drag them

@adjustHint.description: On the subtitle area's frame, shown to find it.

@dragSubtitles.description: For assistive technology: the area that drags the subtitles.

@resizeWidth.description: For assistive technology: a handle that resizes the subtitle area.

lockedToast: Locked. To move them again, unlock them from the menu bar or settings.

@startTranslating.description: Button, and tooltip of the subtitles' toolbar.

lockTooltip: Lock: only the text stays, and clicks go through

@noticeRetry.description: Where the subtitles show, after an error stopped translating.

noticeSlowNetwork: The network is unstable: subtitles may come late. Check your network or proxy.

@noticeSlowNetwork.description: Where the subtitles show, while translating: the cloud recognition's network is slow, its text comes late.

@noticePaused.description: Where the subtitles show, while paused from their toolbar.

@noticeStatus.description: Where the subtitles show, while translating gets ready.

@noticeListening.description: Where the subtitles show, for a few seconds after listening starts.

noticeReady: Tomoru is ready · press {keys} to translate

@noticeReady.description: Where the subtitles show, for a few seconds after the app opens without translating.

@noticeStopped.description: Where the subtitles show, for a few seconds after translating stops.

sampleNoteRunning: Sample subtitles · when someone speaks, subtitles show here

@sampleNoteRunning.description: Over sample subtitles, after the first-run guide, while listening.

@sampleNoteIdle.description: Over sample subtitles, while not translating.

errUnsupportedLocale: Speech recognition on this Mac doesn't support the spoken language.
errAssets: Couldn't download speech recognition for this language.
guideWelcomeBody: Turns what your computer plays into bilingual subtitles.

@allow.description: Button of the first-run guide: have the system ask for the permission.

@openSystemSettings.description: Button of the first-run guide; on the home page and menu bar panel, by the error saying the app may not hear the system.

@guidePermissionTitle.description: The permission page of the first-run guide.

accessNoteAsking: Choose Allow in the window the system shows.

@accessNoteAsking.description: Under the permission, while the system asks.

accessNoteDenied: In System Settings › Privacy & Security › Screen & System Audio Recording, turn on Tomoru under System Audio Recording Only, then reopen Tomoru.

@accessNoteDenied.description: Under the permission, when it is off. Name the settings as System Settings does in the language.

@systemAudioOnly.description: The permission's name, as System Settings lists it.

systemAudioOnlyDescription: Hears only what your computer plays
asrDownloadFailedNote: Recognition didn't download; it tries again when translating starts.

@asrDownloadFailedNote.description: Under Apple's speech recognition, when preparing it failed.

asrFirstDownload: The first time, recognition for it downloads in about 20 s. No need to wait.

@asrFirstDownload.description: Under Apple's speech recognition, while preparing it.

@statusLoadingModel.description: While the on-device translation model loads, before listening.

errModelMissing: The on-device model isn't downloaded. Download it in Settings › Speech & translation.
errNoEndpoint: The translation API chosen was deleted.

@needsMemory.description: After a translation model's size, on a Mac: the memory it needs to run.

@needsVram.description: After a translation model's size, on Windows: the graphics card's memory it needs to run.

asrNeedsMemory: Runs on the GPU, needs {gb} GB of memory

@asrNeedsMemory.description: After a recognition model's size, on a Mac: that it runs on the GPU, and the memory it needs, unlike SenseVoice, which runs on the CPU.

asrNeedsVram: Runs on the graphics card, best with {gb} GB of video memory or more

@asrNeedsVram.description: After a recognition model's size, on Windows: that it runs on the graphics card, and the video memory it wants, unlike SenseVoice, which runs on the CPU.

guideEnginesLater: You can change this any time in Settings.

@guideEnginesLater.description: Under the title of the guide's recognition and translation steps.

guideMtLater: Start with the cloud. Or download an on-device model now: it downloads in the background and takes over once it's done.

@guideMtLater.description: The guide's translation step, under its title: the cloud first; a local model downloads meanwhile without blocking the guide.

meteredNote: You're on a metered connection: downloading uses {size} of data.

@meteredNote.description: Under a model to download, on a metered connection.

offlineNote: You're offline: the cloud and translation APIs need the internet; on-device models work offline.

@offlineNote.description: Over the translation engines, while offline.

@downloadResume.description: Button that goes on with a download stopped before; how much is in shows beside it.

@verifying.description: While a downloaded model's checksum is checked.

downloadDamaged: The download was damaged, and was deleted. Try again.

@downloadDamaged.description: Under a model whose download was damaged.

noSpace: Not enough disk space: {size} is needed.

@noSpace.description: Under a model that does not fit on the disk.

@downloadFailed.description: Under a model whose download failed.

@delete.description: Button: deletes a downloaded model, or a translation API.

@addEndpoint.description: Button that adds a translation API, and that dialog's title.

endpointIntro: Works with OpenAI-compatible APIs, such as DeepSeek or Ollama.

@endpointIntro.description: Under the title of the dialog that adds or edits a translation API: which APIs work.

@endpointName.description: A field of a translation API.

@endpointUrl.description: A field of a translation API.

@endpointModel.description: A field of a translation API.

@endpointKey.description: A field of a translation API.

@endpointKeyKeep.description: Placeholder of the API key, when one is kept.

@endpointFormat.description: A field of a translation API: how the model is prompted.

@endpointFormatChat.description: A prompt format: for general chat models.

@test.description: Button that translates a sample with the API being edited.

@testSucceeded.description: The test translated the sample, in so many milliseconds. Its translation shows under it.

@readsPictures.description: Under a translation API's test result: a picture sent with the sample was translated, so it can translate pictures.

@readsNoPictures.description: Under a translation API's test result: the API refused a picture sent with the sample, so it is not offered for pictures.

@picturesToCloud.description: Under a translation API's test result, when the test found that the API chosen for pictures can't read them: pictures are now translated by the cloud engine, name.

@testFailed.description: The test failed, after so many milliseconds. Why shows under it.

@testNoTranslation.description: Why a test failed: the response had no translation in it.

testOnlyThinking: The model only returned its reasoning process. Use a standard non-reasoning chat model instead.

@testOnlyThinking.description: Why a test failed: a reasoning model spent its answer thinking.

@endpointDeleted.description: A toast after deleting a translation API, beside an Undo button.

@endpointDeletedInUse.description: A toast after deleting the translation API in use, beside an Undo button: translating stops until another is chosen.

@endpointSaved.description: A toast after saving a translation API.

@undo.description: The button of a toast that takes back what was just done.

@modelDeleted.description: A toast after deleting a local translation model.

@modelsFolder.description: On the Speech & Translation page: the title of the row saying where the local models are kept.

@modelsFolderChange.description: Button: choose another folder for the local models, which move there.

@modelsMoving.description: Under the progress bar while the local models move to another folder.

@modelsMoved.description: A toast once the local models are in the folder chosen.

@modelsMoveFailed.description: Why the local models could not be moved; they stay where they were.

errModelsMoving: The on-device models are being moved. Try again when it's done.
errModelBusy: Another on-device model is translating the subtitles, and one runs at a time.

@errModelBusy.description: The picture's card, when its on-device model can't run: the subtitles are being translated by another on-device model.

@reopenApp.description: Guide, permission step: quits and opens the app again, which a permission turned on in System Settings needs.

@guideTryTitle.description: Guide, the step where the user tries translating for real.

guideTryBody: Play a video in {language}, or have Tomoru say a few sample sentences.

@guideTryBody.description: Guide, try step: under the title. language is the spoken language's name.

@guideTryVideo.description: Guide, try step: under the title, in place of guideTryBody when there are no sample sentences in the spoken language. language is its name.

@playSample.description: Guide, try step: a button that has the system's voice say sample sentences aloud, to be translated.

@stopSample.description: Guide, try step: the button stopping the sample being said.

@tryHearing.description: Guide, try step: the first check, that the app hears the computer's sound.

@tryHearingWait.description: Guide, try step: under the first check, until speech is heard.

@tryRecognizing.description: Guide, try step: the second check, that speech is recognized.

@tryRecognizingWait.description: Guide, try step: under the second check, until text comes.

@tryTranslating.description: Guide, try step: the third check, that the text is translated.

@tryTranslatingWith.description: Guide, try step: under the third check, the translation engine.

@trySuccess.description: Guide, try step: once all three checks pass.

sampleNoVoice: This Mac has no {language} voice to say the sample. Play a video in {language} instead.

@sampleNoVoice.description: Guide, try step: the system has no voice to say the sample in the spoken language.

@tryListening.description: Guide, try step: in the preview, while nothing has been said yet.

@skip.description: Guide: goes on without finishing the step.

guideReadyMenuBar: Click Tomoru's icon in the menu bar to change languages, what to hear, and settings.

@guideReadyMenuBar.description: Guide, last step: where the app is.

guideReadySubtitles: Drag the subtitles where you like. Locked, clicks go through them.

@guideReadySubtitles.description: Guide, last step: moving and locking the subtitles.

@done.description: Guide, last step: closes the guide.

@retry.description: Guide's try step, home page and menu bar panel: starts translating again after it failed.

modelReadyInUse: {name} is downloaded and now in use

@modelReadyInUse.description: A toast once a model chosen before it downloaded has come in and is used.

modelRunsOnCpu: Runs on the CPU, no GPU needed.

@modelRunsOnCpu.description: Under a model to download that runs on the CPU, as SenseVoice: that it needs no GPU.

errAsrModelMissing: The speech recognition model isn't downloaded. Download it in Settings › Speech & translation.

@errAsrModelMissing.description: Where the subtitles show, when translating can't start: the recognition model chosen isn't downloaded.

@engineQwenAsr.description: The name of the cloud speech recognition: Qwen ASR on Alibaba Cloud Model Studio.

engineQwenAsrDescription: Billed by the length of the audio sent; nothing is sent while nothing plays.

@engineQwenAsrDescription.description: Under the cloud speech recognition: what it sends where, and what it costs.

engineOpenAiDescription: Billed by the length of the speech sent. Services compatible with OpenAI's transcription API work too.

@engineOpenAiDescription.description: Under OpenAI's speech recognition: what it costs, and that compatible services work.

asrCloudIntro: Create an API key in the Alibaba Cloud Model Studio console.

@asrCloudIntro.description: Under the API key field of Qwen ASR on Alibaba Cloud: where to get one, asrCloudConsole linking there.

asrOpenAiIntro: Create an API key on the OpenAI platform, or use one of a service compatible with its transcription API.

@asrOpenAiIntro.description: Under the API key field of OpenAI's recognition: where to get one, asrOpenAiPlatform linking there.

@asrCloudHost.description: A field's name: the domain of the cloud recognition service.

asrCloudHostDescription: Empty for Beijing; dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com for Singapore, or your workspace's domain.

@asrCloudHostDescription.description: Under the address field of the cloud recognition dialog.

asrOpenAiHostDescription: Empty for OpenAI; for a compatible service, the base URL of its API.

@asrOpenAiHostDescription.description: Under the address field of the dialog setting up OpenAI's speech recognition.

asrOpenAiModelDescription: Empty for live transcription. A model of the transcription API, gpt-transcribe or a compatible service's, is more accurate, and shows each sentence once it ends.

@asrOpenAiModelDescription.description: Under the model field of the dialog setting up OpenAI's speech recognition: what leaving it empty does, and what a model of the transcription API does.

errAsrCloudKey: Cloud recognition has no API key. Set it up in Settings › Speech & translation.

@errAsrCloudKey.description: Where the subtitles show, when translating can't start: the cloud recognition chosen has no API key.

errAsrCloudAuth: Model Studio refused the API key. Check it in Settings › Speech & translation.

@errAsrCloudAuth.description: Where the subtitles show, and in the cloud recognition dialog's test: the service refused the API key.

errAsrApiAuth: The recognition service refused the API key. Check it in Settings › Speech & translation.

@errAsrApiAuth.description: Where the subtitles show, and in the cloud recognition dialog's test: OpenAI's service, or a compatible one, refused the API key.

errAsrBehind: Speech recognition couldn't keep up with what's playing. Choose a lighter model in Settings › Speech & translation, or check the network.

@errAsrBehind.description: Why translating stopped: on-device recognition, or a transcription API, decoded slower than the audio played until about 25 seconds piled up (a model too heavy for the computer, a hung model server, or a slow network).

@errAsrCloud.description: Where the subtitles show, when the cloud recognition failed.

@tabScenes.description: A tab of the settings: the translation scenes, what the user watches, each with its own languages and names.

@scene.description: Label of the menu that chooses the translation scene in use.

@sceneGeneral.description: The translation scene used when the user chose none.

@newScene.description: Button that adds a translation scene; also the new scene's name until the user names it.

noScenes: No scenes of your own yet. Make one for a show, game or meeting you watch often, with its own languages and names.

@noScenes.description: Under the scenes' list while it has only the general scene: what a scene is for. The New Scene button is in the page's header.

@sceneName.description: Label of a translation scene's name.

@sceneAbout.description: Label of a translation scene's description: what the user watches in it.

sceneAboutPlaceholder: e.g. The Apothecary Diaries, with Maomao and Jinshi

@sceneAboutPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of a translation scene's description.

@useScene.description: Button that makes the translation scene being edited the one in use.

@sceneInUse.description: Beside a translation scene being edited, when it is the one in use.

@deletedItem.description: A toast after deleting a translation scene or a name, beside an Undo button.

@termTgt.description: Field of a name in a scene's glossary: its translation.

noTermsYet: No names yet. Add one by hand; once this scene has history, you can learn them from it too.

@keepHistory.description: Switch that keeps the subtitles of each session on this Mac.

historyOff: Subtitles aren't being kept. Turn it on to keep what's translated, on this computer only.

noHistory: Play a video or some audio, and the subtitles translated will show here.

historySceneEmpty: No subtitles kept for this scene yet

@styleLook.description: A card of the subtitle style page: the background, edges, alignment and font.

@styleText.description: A card of the subtitle style page: sizes and colors.

@styleShow.description: A card of the subtitle style page: what shows, and when.

@addApi.description: The last tile of the cloud translation: add an API of one's own.

@useEngine.description: For assistive technology: the radio button beside an engine in the list, which uses it.

@keySaved.description: The end of a cloud recognition service's line once set up, after its model and address.

@modelSizes.description: Heading of a model's sizes, in its detail.

@service.description: Heading of a cloud service's row, in its detail.

@supportedLanguages.description: Heading of the languages a recognition engine hears, in its detail.

@downloaded.description: A tag beside a size of a model that is downloaded.

tooLarge: Needs {need} GB of memory; this computer has {has} GB

@tooLarge.description: Under a size of a model this computer can't run, in red: the memory it needs, and what the computer has.

tooLargeGpu: Needs {need} GB of video memory; this computer has {has} GB

@tooLargeGpu.description: Under a size of a model this computer's graphics card can't run, in red: the video memory it needs, and what the card has.

@notSetUp.description: A cloud recognition service's row, before it is set up.

@modelDownloaded.description: A toast once a model has downloaded, beside a button that uses it.

@downloadModel.description: Button beside a model to download, whose size its tag says.

@appearance.description: A setting of Preferences: light, dark, or as the system is.

@prefsLook.description: A card of Preferences: the appearance and the language the app shows.

@prefsStart.description: A card of Preferences: what happens at launch, and the shortcut.

@appearanceSystem.description: An appearance: light or dark as the system is.

@moveSubtitles.description: Menu bar panel, an icon's tooltip: shows the subtitle area's frame, to move it even while no subtitles show; unlocks them first.

@lockSubtitles.description: Menu bar panel, the open lock's tooltip: locks the subtitles where they are, so clicks pass through them.

@unlockSubtitles.description: Menu bar panel, the shut lock's tooltip while the subtitles are locked: unlocks them, to hover and move them again.

@translateScreen.description: Menu bar panel, an icon's tooltip, followed by its shortcut: has the user select a part of the screen, and translates it; the picture on the clipboard when the app may not capture the screen. Also in the menu bar icon's menu.

@openTomoru.description: Menu bar panel, an icon's tooltip: opens the app's window. Also in the menu bar icon's menu.

@termCount.description: How many names a scene's glossary has.

sceneAboutHint: Sent with each line to translate (not to the on-device 2B model), and used when learning names

@sceneAboutHint.description: Beside a scene's description: what uses it.

@sceneLangs.description: A scene's languages, spoken and translated into.

@learnFromRecords.description: Button of a scene: learns names from its sessions kept.

@moreActions.description: Button opening a menu of more actions.

@newTerm.description: Button adding a row to a scene's glossary.

@termHeardHint.description: Placeholder of the ways a name was misheard.

@termHeardSep.description: What separates the ways a name was misheard, as shown.

@termLearned.description: Tooltip of a name learned from the history, not added by hand.

@dayToday.description: A day of the history's list.

@dayYesterday.description: A day of the history's list.

termFixed: Heard as “{heard}”, corrected by the names

@termFixed.description: Under a line kept: recognition heard a name wrong, and the glossary corrected it.

@recordSource.description: What a session kept heard: an app.

@orderLabel.description: A setting of the subtitles' text: which line is on top.

@askDeleteModel.description: Asks before deleting a local model.

askDeleteModelDetail: To use it again, it downloads again ({size}).

@askDeleteModelDetail.description: Under askDeleteModel: deleting a model can't be undone.

@askDeleteModelInUse.description: Under askDeleteModel, for a model in use: what takes over from it, and that deleting it can't be undone.

askDeleteModelLast: It's in use now, and nothing else recognizes speech until you set one up. To use it again, it downloads again ({size}).

@askDeleteModelLast.description: Under askDeleteModel, for the recognition model in use when nothing else can recognize: that subtitles stop, and that deleting it can't be undone.

@askDiscard.description: Asks, in a dialog's buttons' place, before closing it with changes not saved.

@keepEditing.description: Button beside askDiscard: goes back to the dialog.

@discard.description: Red button beside askDiscard: closes the dialog without saving.

@imageTitle.description: The title of the card that shows a picture's translation, and of the group in Speech & Translation that sets up translating pictures.

@imageTranslating.description: The picture's card, until the translation comes.

imageNoText: No translation came back: the picture may have no text.

@imageNoText.description: The picture's card, when the model sent no translation.

imageFailed: Couldn't translate this picture. Try again in a moment.

@imageFailed.description: The picture's card, when translating it failed; the error is under it.

imageNote: Powered by Index-Translate, in the cloud

@imageNote.description: The picture's card, at its foot: what translates the picture. "Index-Translate" is a link to its page.

imageNoteLocal: Powered by Index-Translate, on this computer

@imageNoteLocal.description: The picture's card, at its foot, when a local model translates it. "Index-Translate" is a link to its page.

@imageNoteEndpoint.description: The picture's card, at its foot, when a translation API the user added translates it.

imageEndpointFailed: {name} couldn't translate this picture. It may not read pictures.

@imageEndpointFailed.description: The picture's card, when the user's translation API failed to translate it: it may not read pictures, and no other engine is asked. The API's error is under it.

imageKept: Neither the picture nor its translation is kept.

@imageKept.description: The tooltip of the picture card's foot.

@imageZoomIn.description: The tooltip of the picture's thumbnail on its card: clicked, the picture shows whole, as large as it was on the screen.

@copied.description: The Copy button for a moment after a click.

@imageShortcut.description: Settings, General: the shortcut that translates the picture on the clipboard.

@shortcutDuplicate.description: A shortcut recorded that the other shortcut of the app already is.

screenSelectWhy: Needs Screen Recording. Only what you select is captured.

@screenSelectTurnOn.description: Button that asks for Screen Recording, to select a part of the screen.

@screenSelectAsking.description: The button while the system asks the user for Screen Recording.

@imageEngine.description: Speech & translation, the Picture Translation group: the row choosing the engine that translates pictures, from a menu of those that read them.

@imageShortcutRow.description: Speech & translation, the Picture Translation group: the row of the shortcut that translates a picture (imageShortcut in Preferences).

@guidePhaseSetup.description: Guide: the first phase, choosing languages, permissions and engines.

@guidePhaseTry.description: Guide: the second phase, trying subtitles, pictures and the shortcuts.

@guidePhaseStart.description: Guide: the last phase, where the app is then.

@privacyTitle.description: Guide, permissions: the card on the right about privacy.

privacySoundDetail: What your Mac plays is only turned into live subtitles, and not kept.
privacyScreenDetail: Only a screenshot you take yourself is translated, and it's gone once translated.
privacyHistoryDetail: Subtitles aren't kept unless you turn it on, and then only here.

@guideShortcutsTitle.description: Guide: the step with the shortcuts.

guideShortcutsBody: Press it anywhere to start or stop translating. Try it now.

@guideSelectTitle.description: Guide: the step that offers selecting text on screen to translate.

guideSelectAsk: Press a shortcut and select text on screen to see it translated. Want it?

@guideSelectAsk.description: Guide, selecting step: what it is, before it is on.

guideSelectSettings: Turn on Tomoru under Screen & System Audio Recording in System Settings. When asked to reopen Tomoru, click Later.

@guideSelectSettings.description: Guide, selecting step: once asked, it is turned on in System Settings.

guideSelectIntro: Follow the two steps below to try a real translation.

@guideSelectIntro.description: The guide's select-to-translate step, once it is on: what to do, over its two checks.

@guideSelectPress.description: The first check of the select-to-translate step: press the shortcut once.

guideSelectFrame: Press it again and select the dialogue on the right

@guideSelectFrame.description: The second check of the select-to-translate step, once the shortcut works: press it again and select the sample dialogue on the stage, which is translated for real.

guideSelectAllow: The first time, macOS asks again: click Allow.

@guideSelectAllow.description: Under the second check, on a Mac: macOS asks again the first time.

@guideSelectHere.description: Over the sample dialogue on the guide's stage, until it is selected.

@shortcutWorks.description: Guide: under a shortcut, once pressed right.

@showInFinder.description: Button of a session kept: shows its file in Finder.

@tabStats.description: The statistics page, in the sidebar.

@statsRange.description: Statistics page: names the choice of period.

statsEmpty: Nothing yet. Play a video or some audio while translating, and this shows how long, how much and how fast.

@statsEmpty.description: The statistics while nothing was ever translated.

@statsActivity.description: Home page: the card of a square a day, deeper for more lines, from the week Tomoru was first used.

@statsLess.description: Home page: the light end of the daily squares' legend.

@statsMore.description: Home page: the deep end of the daily squares' legend.

@homeOpenStats.description: Home page: the button by the lines by day that goes to the statistics page.

@openEngines.description: Home page and menu bar panel: the button by an error that goes to the Speech & translation page, where it is fixed. Name the page as the sidebar does.

@statRun.description: Listening time across the selected period, including silence.

@unitHours.description: Unit after a number of hours.

@statsDaily.description: Statistics page: the chart's title, by day.

@statsMonthly.description: Statistics page: the chart's title, by month.

@statsChartShows.description: Statistics page: names the choice of what the chart shows.

@statsUsage.description: Statistics page: the card of how much speech recognition or translation did, by engine.

@statsLatency.description: Statistics page: the card of how long each step takes.

@latFinal.description: A latency: from a word spoken to recognition settling on it.

latFinalDescription: From a word spoken to the recognizer settling on it

@latFirstTranslation.description: A latency: from a line showing to the first words of its translation.

latFirstTranslationDescription: From a line showing to the first words of its translation, waiting for the lines before it included

@latTranslation.description: A latency: from a line showing to its translation done.

latTranslationDescription: From a line showing to its translation done

@latEndToEnd.description: A latency: from the end of a sentence's speech to the first words of its translation.

latEndToEndDescription: From the end of a sentence to the first words of its translation: what you wait

@latP90.description: Under a latency: the time 90% of them came within.

@statsSpread.description: Statistics page, the latency card: shows how a latency's times spread, as a histogram.

@latYouWait.description: Statistics page, over the latency of what the user waits: from the end of speech to its translation.

@latHalf.description: Statistics page, on a latency's histogram: the median.

latNone: Not timed in this period yet

@latNone.description: Statistics page: a latency chosen that has no times in the period.

@statsVsBefore.description: Statistics page, under the total: how much more or less than in as many days before the period.

@latFaster.description: Statistics page, by a latency: its median is this much shorter than in as many days before the period.

@latSlower.description: Statistics page, by a latency: its median is this much longer than in as many days before the period.

latSame: About as fast as the {n} days before

@latSame.description: Statistics page, by a latency: its median is about what it was in as many days before the period.

@unitSeconds.description: Unit after a number of seconds.

@engineUnknown.description: Statistics page: what was counted before Tomoru noted the engines.

@useChars.description: Statistics page, of a translator: the letters of its translations.

@useImages.description: How many pictures were translated, on the statistics' Translation side, after Picture Translation.

@statsPerDay.description: Statistics page, under the total: the average of a day of the period.

@factAudio.description: Statistics page, of a cloud recognizer: names the minutes of audio sent, which it bills.

@factInTokens.description: Statistics page, of a translator: names the input tokens it took, as the service counted them.

@factOutTokens.description: Statistics page, of a translator: names the output tokens it took, as the service counted them.

@factFailed.description: Statistics page, of a translator: names the lines it failed.

@shortcutNeedsModifierWin.description: Shortcut field, on Windows: a key alone cannot be a global shortcut.

lockedToastWin: Locked. To move them again, click Tomoru's icon in the taskbar to unlock them, or unlock them in settings.

@lockedToastWin.description: Over the subtitles, on Windows, once they are locked in place.

sampleNoVoiceWin: Windows has no {language} voice to say the sample. Play a video in {language} instead, or add the voice in Settings › Time & language › Speech.

@sampleNoVoiceWin.description: Guide, try step, on Windows: the system has no voice to say the sample in the spoken language.

guideReadyTray: Click Tomoru's icon in the corner of the taskbar to change languages and what to hear; right-click it to start translating or open settings. If it isn't there, it's under ^.

@guideReadyTray.description: Guide, last step, on Windows: where the app is afterwards.

@showInExplorer.description: Button of a session kept, on Windows: shows its file in File Explorer.

@engineNone.description: In use, where no speech recognition is chosen yet (Windows has none of its own).

errNoAsr: Choose speech recognition first, a model or the cloud, in Settings › Speech & translation.

@errNoAsr.description: Translating could not start: no speech recognition is chosen yet.

guideAsrChoose: Choose a model to run on this computer. It downloads when you choose it.

@guideAsrChoose.description: Guide, engines step, where the system has no speech recognition: what to choose.

tryModelThen: Translating starts once it is downloaded.

@tryModelDownloading.description: The guide's try step, while the recognition model chosen is still downloading.

@engineHyMtCloudDescription.description: Under Hy-MT2 on Tencent Cloud, in the settings: what it costs.

mtHyMtIntro: Create an API key in the Tencent Cloud TokenHub console.

@mtHyMtIntro.description: Under the API key field of Hy-MT2 on Tencent Cloud: where to get one, mtHyMtConsole linking there.

errMtCloudKey: Cloud translation has no API key. Set it up in Settings › Speech & translation.

@errMtCloudKey.description: Where the subtitles show, when a cloud translation service is chosen without its API key.

@asrCloudConsole.description: The part of asrCloudIntro that links to the console's API key page: word for word as it is there.

@asrOpenAiPlatform.description: The part of asrOpenAiIntro that links to OpenAI's API key page: word for word as it is there.

@mtHyMtConsole.description: The part of mtHyMtIntro that links to TokenHub's API key page: word for word as it is there.

@engineCloudSize.description: A smaller size of Index-Translate in the cloud, by its size (9B): said to be the cloud's, as there are local ones of that size.

@engineIndexCloud.description: Index-Translate in the cloud, its sizes together, in the settings' list of engines: by who serves it, as the other cloud services are.

@linkTokenHub.description: A small button at the top right of Hy-MT2 on Tencent Cloud's detail, in the settings: opens its model's page on TokenHub. The platform's name, short.

@sizeQuicker.description: Before a model's size and what it needs, in its row in the settings: this size translates or recognizes sooner than the family's other. One or two words.

@sizeMoreAccurate.description: Before a model's size and what it needs, in its row in the settings: this size makes fewer mistakes than the family's other. One or two words.

@runsHere.description: After a model's size, in its row in the settings and the guide: this computer has the memory it needs. Short, plain.

@modelAndAddress.description: A fold under a cloud service's API key, in the settings: opens its model and address fields, which most leave as they are.

@feedback.description: About: the row giving feedback, a problem or an idea, and the title of its dialog.

feedbackHint: A problem or an idea, with an AI agent or on GitHub

@feedbackHint.description: About: the note under Feedback & ideas.

@feedbackKind.description: The feedback dialog: the name of its choice between Problem and Idea, for screen readers.

@feedbackProblem.description: The feedback dialog: the segment for something that doesn't work as it should.

@feedbackIdea.description: The feedback dialog: the segment for something Tomoru could do, or do better.

@feedbackOpen.description: About: the button that opens the feedback dialog.

feedbackIntroProblem: Say what went wrong, copy it and paste it into an AI agent like Claude Code or Codex: it looks through the logs with you, and opens the issue on GitHub once you say yes.

@feedbackIntroProblem.description: The feedback dialog with Problem chosen: under its title.

feedbackIntroIdea: Say what you'd like Tomoru to do, copy it and paste it into an AI agent like Claude Code or Codex: it shapes it into a suggestion with you, and opens the issue on GitHub once you say yes.

@feedbackIntroIdea.description: The feedback dialog with Idea chosen: under its title.

feedbackPlaceholderProblem: e.g. Watching Frieren on Crunchyroll, the subtitles stopped after ten minutes

@feedbackPlaceholderProblem.description: The feedback dialog with Problem chosen: the example in its empty text box.

feedbackPlaceholderIdea: e.g. Watching Frieren, I'd like to save an episode's subtitles as an SRT file

@feedbackPlaceholderIdea.description: The feedback dialog with Idea chosen: the example in its empty text box.

@feedbackSummary.description: The feedback dialog: the title over what goes with the user's words.

@feedbackVersion.description: The feedback dialog: the app's version, beside "Tomoru 0.1.4".

@feedbackSystem.description: The feedback dialog: the system's name and version, beside "macOS 26.1".

@feedbackEngines.description: The feedback dialog: recognition and translation, beside "Apple → Index-Translate cloud".

@feedbackLangs.description: The feedback dialog: the languages translated, beside "Japanese → Chinese".

feedbackPrivate: No API keys, subtitles or recordings

@feedbackPrivate.description: The feedback dialog: beside a lock, under what goes with the user's words.

@feedbackShow.description: The feedback dialog: a fold showing the whole text copied.

@feedbackOnGitHub.description: The feedback dialog: opens GitHub's issue form, started with what the user wrote and the app's setup.

@feedbackCopy.description: The feedback dialog: copies the user's words with the app's setup and a guide for an AI agent.
